sections.kicker: Prepared for Galpão Tecidos by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Galpão Tecidos describes its category. Its real customer, the one who sews, is named by someone else.
sections.keep: Your close-ups of fabric. The fuchsia texture is the most striking image on the grid.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.what: The bio names the category, not the person it is for.
pins.why: Every fabric shop writes this. The line that fits you, a place for people who sew and create, appears only in a partner's caption.
pins.how: Write the bio to the creator and let the fabric support it.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: A new customer sees one more fabric shop in Fortaleza.

pins.area: Fuchsia fabric, black logo tile, yellow and cream layouts in one grid
pins.what: Each post gets a different layout, so the fabric does not lead.
pins.why: The textures are your best asset. The changing type and colors around them hide it.
pins.how: Fix one layout and let a fabric close-up lead every post.
pins.label: Your grid
pins.cost: The feed looks like several shops, not one place to be inspired.

pins.quote: Conte-nos, mostre-nos suas criaturas e suas histórias como criadores.
pins.what: You ask customers to show what they made, and the grid shows none of it.
pins.why: What your customers make is the proof that no other fabric shop has.
pins.how: Give customer pieces the grid and keep your fabric as the supporting shot.
pins.label: Your grid
pins.cost: You keep the best evidence out of sight.
